polaris: RP nickelates: is density-wave-driven layer decoupling a superconducting precursor or a superconductivity suppressor?
framework: Anisotropic coherent-incoherent interlayer transport in multiorbital layered correlated metals; the organizing variable is Ni dz2-assisted interlayer electronic coherence, diagnosed by rho_perp/rho_parallel and effective current penetration depth.
findings: Round 1 literature-driven conclusion: the published evidence supports a distinction between static DW order and DW fluctuations. Static DW order in La4Ni3O10 is not a superconducting precursor at the same mechanism level; it suppresses the Ni dz2-mediated interlayer channel, increases transport anisotropy, and therefore acts as a suppressor of the three-dimensional phase-coherent superconducting state. A weaker precursor statement remains possible only for precritical spin/charge fluctuations after the static layer-decoupling order is collapsed by pressure. The first quantitative discriminator is whether a tuning path reduces rho_perp/rho_parallel and restores coherent c-axis transport before or at superconducting onset.
weakest_link: The inference compares ambient-pressure DW electrodynamics with pressure-induced superconductivity. Pressure changes lattice, orbital energies, spin correlations, and carrier coherence simultaneously, so layer coherence is a strongly supported organizing parameter but not yet a uniquely isolated causal variable.
next_plan: Round 2 should separate static DW order from DW fluctuations by compiling pressure-dependent rho_perp/rho_parallel, optical Drude weight, and DW amplitude data. The decisive test is whether superconductivity appears only after the c-axis coherent channel recovers, even if DW fluctuations remain strong.

claims.statement: Static DW order in La4Ni3O10 is a layer-coherence suppressor: below T_DW it sharply increases rho_c/rho_ab and reduces the effective c-axis current penetration depth.

equations.label: F1
equations.description: Resistivity anisotropy used as the experimental proxy for loss of interlayer coherence.

equations.label: F2
equations.description: Large-anisotropy current penetration depth from flux-transformer/six-terminal anisotropic transport analysis.

limits.desc: current confined near the driven surface as layers decouple

assumptions: rho_c/rho_ab or rho_perp/rho_parallel is a valid proxy for interlayer electronic coherence.
The optically extrapolated DC anisotropy and direct DC anisotropy are comparable diagnostics of the same c-axis channel.
The relevant interlayer channel is dominated by Ni dz2-apical-oxygen hybridization.

claims.statement: A DW-glue precursor scenario can coexist with the data only if it is assigned to fluctuations, not to the static ordered DW state that reconstructs dz2 occupancy and suppresses c-axis transport.

equations.description: Dimensionless suppressor index: static DW gap/reconstruction scale over effective interlayer coherence scale. Superconductivity-friendly regime requires S to decrease under tuning.

assumptions: The optical DW gap 2Delta_DW = 112 meV can be used as an order-of-magnitude static reconstruction scale.
Pressure-induced superconductivity requires at least partial recovery of interlayer phase stiffness.
Pairing glue and phase-coherence organizer are separable roles.

claims.statement: The first data-level decision rule is: if pressure raises Tc while decreasing gamma_rho or increasing c-axis Drude weight, DW layer decoupling is a suppressor; if Tc rises while gamma_rho remains high and c-axis coherence stays lost, the precursor scenario gains support.

equations.label: F4
equations.description: Observable discriminator for pressure or strain tuning. D > 1 with decreasing gamma supports recovered interlayer coherence as superconductivity organizer.

limits.desc: no coherence recovery; Tc change cannot be attributed to reduced anisotropy
unphysical but flags that the formula is valid only for positive measured anisotropy

assumptions: A comparable gamma_rho can be measured under pressure or approximated from pressure-dependent optical Drude weights.
Ambient Tc is effectively zero for the bulk single-crystal state considered here.
The discriminator is empirical and does not replace microscopic pairing calculations.

derivation_chain.literature_anchor: Guan et al. 2026 PRL reports La4Ni3O10 optical/DC anisotropy changing from about 70 at room temperature to about 2600 at 4 K, with the strongest enhancement at T_DW.
derivation_chain.derivation: Define gamma_rho = rho_perp/rho_parallel. The observed gamma increase is 2600/70 = 37.14, so the DW state moves the system toward the electronically decoupled-layer limit.

inspector_check.direction: DW order increases gamma_rho and suppresses interlayer transport.
inspector_check.assumptions: Optically extrapolated DC rho values track the low-energy coherent transport channel.

derivation_chain.literature_anchor: Liu et al. 2026 arXiv gives the six-terminal anisotropic transport relation and the large-anisotropy penetration-depth approximation z_eff = L/pi*sqrt(rho_parallel/rho_perp).
derivation_chain.derivation: Using L = 1.0 mm and gamma = 2600 gives z_eff = 6.24 micrometer; using gamma = 70 gives z_eff = 38.0 micrometer. The DW state therefore confines current about six times closer to the driven surface, consistent with layer decoupling.

inspector_check.direction: Larger gamma_rho reduces z_eff and operationally measures loss of c-axis coherence.
inspector_check.data: arXiv:2605.18524 equations (1)-(2) and text after them; PRL 136, 216501 anisotropy values.
inspector_check.assumptions: Sample length of 1 mm is within the reported 0.8-1.1 mm range.

derivation_chain.literature_anchor: Xu et al. 2025 Nat Commun reports collapse of DW and emergence of superconductivity in pressurized La4Ni3O10; Liu et al. 2026 reports an inverse correlation between ambient anisotropy and maximum pressure-induced Tc across RP nickelates.
derivation_chain.derivation: If superconductivity appears as the static DW collapses and if higher Tc correlates with lower anisotropy, the conservative inference is that static DW order is a suppressor of superconducting coherence, while fluctuations remain a separate possible pairing channel.

inspector_check.direction: Tc enhancement accompanied by gamma reduction supports the suppressor interpretation.
inspector_check.assumptions: Pressure does not create superconductivity solely through a variable independent of interlayer coherence.

landing_calculation.type: A: concrete numerical prediction from existing experimental system
landing_calculation.system: bulk single-crystal La4Ni3O10 measured in PRL 136, 216501 and six-terminal geometry scale reported in arXiv:2605.18524
landing_calculation.prediction: For a 1.0 mm long La4Ni3O10 bar, the DW-state anisotropy gamma_rho = 2600 implies z_eff = 6.24 micrometer; above-DW gamma_rho = 70 implies z_eff = 38.0 micrometer. Any pressure path that turns on bulk superconductivity while keeping z_eff below about 10 micrometer would contradict the layer-coherence suppressor hypothesis; recovery toward tens of micrometers supports it.
landing_calculation.reanalysis_target: PRL 136, 216501 Fig. 2(e,f) and Zenodo dataset DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20089847; extract temperature-dependent rho_ab and rho_c* to compute z_eff(T).

deepening_1.next_layer_consequence: If static DW suppresses interlayer coherence, the immediate physical consequence is reduced c-axis phase stiffness and reduced Josephson-like locking between Ni-O layers.
deepening_1.second_layer_consequence: Reduced c-axis phase stiffness can lower bulk Tc even if local pairing correlations or spin fluctuations grow; this naturally separates pairing amplitude from global phase coherence.

deepening_2.most_fragile_premise: The most fragile premise is that pressure-induced superconductivity in RP nickelates needs substantial dz2-mediated interlayer coherence rather than only in-plane dx2-y2 pairing plus weak residual phase locking.
deepening_2.if_premise_fails: If in-plane pairing alone can produce the observed high-pressure bulk superconductivity, then DW layer decoupling may be a competing normal-state reconstruction but not the central suppressor. The required check is pressure-axis-resolved c-axis Drude weight or rho_perp/rho_parallel across the superconducting dome.
